data.raw_text:
Spokesperson of the Chinese Embassy Ji Lingpeng: 

1. Since March, the Philippine Navy, Coast Guard, and other government vessels and aircraft have repeatedly provoked incidents of infringement at sea and hyped them up.

On March 18, two Philippine C-208 aircraft illegally intruded into the airspace over China’s Huangyan Dao without approval from the Chinese government. The PLA Southern Theater Command organized naval and air forces to warn and expel them in accordance with the law and regulations.

On March 20, one Philippine C-208 aircraft, again without permission from the Chinese government, illegally entered the airspace near Meiji Jiao in China’s Nansha Qundao. The PLA Southern Theater Command deployed naval and air forces to track, monitor, warn, and expel it in accordance with the law and regulations.

On March 25, the PLA Navy vessel No. 532 was conducting routine patrol operations in waters under China’s jurisdiction near Zhubi Jiao in Nansha Qundao. After detecting a Philippine vessel, the Chinese side issued verbal warnings. Disregarding repeated warnings, the Philippine vessel No. 507 continuously adjusted its course to the right from the port side of the Chinese vessel No. 532, deliberately turning starboard and dangerously approaching the Chinese vessel, thereby interfering with its normal patrol operations. The Chinese vessel adopted professional and standard maneuvers, effectively avoiding any accident. The Philippine vessel’s actions were unsafe and unprofessional, posing a high risk of maritime incidents. Moreover, the Philippine side made counter-accusations, falsely claiming that the Chinese vessel had made a “dangerous approach.”

The Philippine side also falsely alleged that on March 7, the Chinese Navy used fire-control radar to illuminate a Philippine vessel near Xianbin Jiao. Such claims are entirely fabricated and are being used to smear China, confuse public perception, mislead public opinion, and deliberately tarnish China’s image.

2. China has territorial sovereignty over Nansha Qundao and Huangyan Dao and their adjacent waters, and enjoys sovereign rights and jurisdiction in the relevant waters. These rights are consistent with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The actions of the Philippine side infringe upon China’s territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, violate international law including UNCLOS and the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea, undermine maritime navigation safety, and exacerbate tensions at sea. China will never allow the Philippine side to act recklessly, and will continue to take strong measures in accordance with the law and regulations to firmly safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, as well as peace and stability in the South China Sea.

3. The Philippine side first engages in infringement and provocation against China and creates incidents, then fabricates facts and shifts the blame, demonstrating a lack of credibility. The international community can clearly see through the Philippines’ attempts at cognitive manipulation. China will continue to base its position on facts and law, clarify its stance, present the truth, and resolutely counter smears and defamation against it.

4. China’s position on handling disputes with the Philippines in the South China Sea is consistent and clear: it upholds resolving territorial and maritime disputes through negotiation, and properly managing differences and the maritime situation through dialogue. At present, China and the Philippines maintain communication on maritime-related issues through diplomatic channels. The Philippine side should demonstrate sincerity, match words with deeds, immediately cease maritime infringement and provocation, stop hyping up the maritime situation, and return to the correct track of resolving maritime issues through dialogue and consultation
